title: Anthropic's Claude Code Sandbox
content:
Anthropic Open-Sources Claude Code Sandbox Under Apache 2.0
TL;DR
- Anthropic released sandbox-runtime (srt), the OS-level sandbox used in Claude Code, as the @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime npm package under Apache-2.0.
- The runtime uses sandbox-exec with Seatbelt profiles on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux, and an alpha Windows build backed by Windows Filtering Platform filters and NTFS ACLs.
- Documented features include allow-only network policies, Unix-socket allowlisting, experimental TLS termination, credential masking, AWS SigV4 signing, and drop-in sandboxing of MCP servers.
Anthropic has released the sandbox that runs behind Claude Code as an open-source npm package, `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime`, under the Apache-2.0 license. The project README describes srt as "a lightweight sandboxing tool for enforcing filesystem and network restrictions on arbitrary processes at the OS level, without requiring a container."
The runtime wraps each platform's native primitives. On macOS it uses `sandbox-exec` with dynamically generated Seatbelt profiles. On Linux it uses `bubblewrap` with network namespace isolation. The Windows build combines a Windows Filtering Platform egress fence with a write-restricted token and explicit NTFS ACLs, and ships a bundled `srt-win.exe` helper for x64 and arm64. A one-time elevated `windows-install` step provisions a dedicated `srt-sandbox` local user account and the machine-wide WFP filter set.
Features called out in the README include an allow-only network policy with wildcard domain support, Unix-socket allowlisting, experimental TLS termination for MITM inspection of HTTPS, credential masking for environment variables and files, and AWS SigV4 request signing with masked keys. The docs show drop-in MCP server sandboxing by swapping the `command` field in an `.mcp.json` entry from `npx` to `srt`.
The repo frames the release as "a research preview developed for Claude Code to enable safer AI agents" and cautions that "APIs and configuration formats may evolve." The Windows backend documents specific holes. Tools built on the system TLS stack (Schannel), including `System32\curl.exe`, PowerShell's `Invoke-WebRequest`, .NET `HttpClient`, and `winget`, cannot be used, and traffic routed through system services such as Windows Update escapes the WFP fence.

Original headline: Anthropic Open-Sources Claude Code's sandbox-runtime Under Apache 2.0 With Linux, macOS, Windows Support

report.summary: Anthropic has open-sourced sandbox-runtime (srt), the OS-level sandboxing layer behind Claude Code, under Apache-2.0 with Linux, macOS, and Windows support.
report.background: AI coding agents like Claude Code run with broad permissions: they read repositories, execute shell commands, install packages, and call external APIs. That power creates an obvious attack surface, since a malicious prompt, compromised dependency, or poisoned MCP server can trick an agent into exfiltrating credentials or overwriting files. Container-based isolation has been the standard answer, but it adds heavy setup friction and breaks on developer laptops. Anthropic's approach leans on primitives already present in each operating system: Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux, and the Windows Filtering Platform plus NTFS ACLs on Windows. Releasing the layer as a standalone npm package signals a shift from proprietary safety infrastructure toward shared public tooling. It also arrives amid wider industry debate over agent security, following several high-profile prompt-injection and supply-chain incidents targeting coding assistants, and competition from open agent frameworks that need credible sandboxing stories.
key_points: No container required: srt applies filesystem and network restrictions to arbitrary processes using native OS sandboxing primitives, wrapping Seatbelt profiles on macOS and bubblewrap network namespaces on Linux. This keeps setup light enough for ordinary developer machines while still limiting what a misbehaving agent can touch.

Network policy is allow-only: outbound traffic is denied unless destinations are explicitly allowlisted, with wildcard domain support and Unix-socket allowlisting. Optional experimental TLS termination enables HTTPS inspection, and credential masking plus AWS SigV4 signing keep secrets out of agent context while still permitting signed cloud calls.

MCP servers get drop-in sandboxing: developers can swap the command field in an .mcp.json entry from npx to srt, isolating third-party tool servers with no code changes. Given how often MCP servers run untrusted code with broad access, this is a practical, low-friction hardening step.

Windows support is real but incomplete: the alpha backend needs a one-time elevated install that creates a dedicated srt-sandbox user and machine-wide filters. Tools using the Schannel TLS stack such as System32 curl.exe, PowerShell's Invoke-WebRequest, .NET HttpClient, and winget are blocked, and traffic through system services like Windows Update escapes the fence.

It is explicitly a research preview: Anthropic warns that APIs and configuration formats may evolve, and the documentation openly lists gaps rather than overclaiming. Treating srt as production-grade isolation today would be premature.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is a meaningful precedent: a leading lab publishing its agent safety layer under a permissive license turns internal security work into shared infrastructure and raises expectations for competitors. For developers, srt offers a low-friction way to run coding agents and third-party MCP servers with tighter blast radius, without Docker or VM overhead, and it can sandbox any process, not just Claude. But the documented Windows gaps matter: anyone relying on Schannel-based tools or system-service traffic should treat coverage as partial and layer additional controls. For regular users, the benefit is indirect but real — agents handling their repositories and credentials become less likely to leak data or destroy files. The bigger takeaway is cultural: transparent, inspectable sandboxing is becoming a baseline requirement rather than a differentiator.
report.tools: Install @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime from npm and read its README for platform-specific setup. Watch the upstream primitives it builds on: bubblewrap on Linux and Seatbelt/sandbox-exec on macOS. Compare with container-based options like Docker's sandboxing or gVisor and Firecracker for stronger isolation. For agent security more broadly, follow the MCP specification and reference servers, plus emerging prompt-injection defenses such as CaMeL-style capability controls. Also track Anthropic's Claude Code documentation for how srt defaults evolve.
